english: Either frustration or... something else.
Excitement? No. It couldn't be...
However, there is work to be done. You are busy as well.
That's true, but-
The halo comes to a stop.
She is attempting to focus.
Let us- reconvene. We shall reconvene, Cleric.
Re-convene?
Wait... that means you're convening!
We're convening?
Okay. Alright. (Get all giddy.)
One of her many eyes turns back to you.
We are convening.
Alert, alert! <shake>Convening</shake> is happening!
This is it. You have done it.
You have become the convenionator.
<shake>Convening</shake>. Is. Good.
We're convening!
Convention is happening. I see.
(Raise your eyebrows, without her being able to see it.)
Wonderful. Simply marvelous.
You've got her right in your Pouch of Holding.
After.
The election.
Her eyes fall back on her papers.
Focus on the tea shop, Cleric.
You live.
That wasn't so bad, eh?
Sometimes you just gotta take a risk like that. Put it all on the line. Women dig that.
<shake>Geezus goose-lording hells...</shake>
That was intense.
The contents of your stomach... are pushing up.
Keep it in, damn you! Now...
Now. Now, you can relax. Go... do whatever you were doing before.
This is embarrassing.
She is but a woman. Despite her celestial appearance. Do not be so flustered.
Being flustered is in the heart of every man, you blue fool.
Be glad.
Be joyful.
For you have risen to the occasion. Your father would be proud.
Why are you doing this to yourself?
You feel as if the world is against you.
This woman... she is simply too powerful, isn't she?
Like, as pertains to planes of existence, yours is in a different league from hers.
The type to crush you like an insect. And yet you're trying to win her favor?
Nah. Not going to happen.
Nah. Not today.
You have no idea what to say. Maybe tomorrow. If you're real lucky.
Oh...
But...
Yeah.
Oh, indeed.
Remember.
This is what happens if you try to speak with women.
You might as well just turn to dust...
No buts. This is serious, you-
Stand up for yourself.
You must. For the good of them all.
YOU HAVE TO STAND UP FOR YOURSELF!
A man does not lie down like this. It doesn't matter how many times you get knocked down, or broken into pieces on the living room floor.
A man takes every failure with the stride the world demands.
He looks the painful realization that the world is against him, and LAUGHS at it.
He laughs at the pain. And he keeps going until it breaks him into dust.
Become dust, brother. That sacrifice is exactly what this world needs.
Dust?
That's...
You do not need to fight so much.
Do you remember what she told you?
The day she ran into the crowd with that scowl on her face.
Oh no. Myran.
It didn't start out violent.
An oppressed mass gathered on that day. It was not an Azgalist-thing.
There was no real Azgalism in those days. Not with the human workers, at least.
Five hundred textile workers. Mostly women - marching the streets in protest of horrendous working conditions. A powder keg, set off by the latest indignity thrust upon them by the factory owners:
A mass of unseen skilled labor. Spawned out of cheap generators.
They did not even employ any wizards to maintain the magic.
Normally these invisible esoteric spirits would not be able to handle the workload of the average textile seamstress - but the simplification of some of the machinery made it suddenly possible.
The women, who lost their livelihoods, were screaming in the streets. As is only natural.

Four years earlier, the Bone Purge made it clear: esoteric production was not the life-blood of Norvik. And considering the dramatic failure of Arcanist methods in the last century, most people agreed on this point.
Alas, greed knows no boundaries.
Myran brought me there.
She did.
That girl did not think about anything but the egalitarian dream.
Huffed up on green pamphlets and green books, she shared that dream with you, along with the rest of that group of outcasts.
You, and a handful of other activists of the Youth held signs, chanted dwarven songs, and held the line - as the fascists rolled in.
I was young. I didn't know any better.
I didn't throw any rocks.
I was only there because of her.
You went the peaceful route. Despite their aggression.
That is true, admittedly.
As the Urthguard peacekeepers pushed into the crowd, bulky pavises breaking bones and dislocating jaws, the group scattered.
One by one, those outcasts left to live in the system, instead of attempting to smash it with an adamantine hammer.
I left, didn't I? Right?
Ah, shit. And I stayed behind like an idiot.
You stood by your principles. Or...
You stood by her principles. She had a lot of those.
When the bricks began to fly, it was far too late to back out. The roaring crowd, surrounded. The batons pelting. The mass crying.
The state won.
That was the last time you saw Myran.
May she rest in peace.
What?
She did not die.
Oh.
Last you heard, she was leading the Azgalian Front. She is their only female Foreperson.
She is one of the most influential women in Norvik.
Ah. That somehow feels worse.
She made something out of herself.
So she never sold out.
Why do I miss her? She didn't give a damn about me.
It is a complicated feeling. One you must keep thinking about until the end of your days.
Yes. She is a woman with aim.
You knew she never would.
Because the first feeling is always the strongest.
The rest are felt with cushions around the heart.
(Open your eyes.)
Ettir is still looking at you.
You meet her gaze.
Perhaps... you should rethink your methods here.
Hm. This whole flirting thing? You can try again later.
Right now, just chill. Okay?
This woman served Urth.
Why?
A woman of her caliber, a great celestial of the west...
She must be bound by some oath.
Urth was just that good of a god, I suppose.
Maybe she likes it here?
Of course. An oath to serve the city, even beyond his death...
Of course he was. But why this celestial in particular?
No. She is clearly miserable.
She is a sister to the cause.
Ask her.
Ask her why she is here.
(Raise your head.)
The angel's many eyes focus on you as you open your mouth.
Why do you remain here? Serving a city of men?
She stops her work. The floating papers begin to move out of the way.
And the angel descends ever so slightly.
It is...
She grits teeth and clenches fists.
The first time you've seen her perform any kind of physical exertion.
Holy shit.
To miasto, gdzie rozum sczezł.
This city has lost its head.
A city of <shake>fools</shake>.
Your body shakes. You hold no power against her.
Your legs shake. You stand before a goddess.
Oh gods, the goblin yelps.
Stand your ground.
Face her.
(Do not lower your head.)
(Lower your head.)
Gods, I just remembered! I've got a... thing.
The goblin hurries down the stairs behind you.
Coward.
He is wise.
The celestial faces you.
My city is not yours to insult, angel.
Norvik is stronger than you think.
You speak truth. This city is lost.
If we're all so damn stupid, then why do you stay here?!
Her normally stone-faced expression is still there, but with a swirling mass of esoteric force where her eyes are supposed to be.
Her telepathic voice rattles louder in your mind.
A crackling boom.
I am not a slave to this city.
A swirling sensation. The eye of a storm.
You feel as though the world is vibrating around you.
The angel's halo slows.
She is calmer now. As if releasing that angry remark was exactly what she has been waiting to do.
But that is not an answer to your question.
No, it's really not.
It's not an easy question to answer.
(Just listen.)
She lifts her head, and the many eyes follow.
Why do I remain here? she asks herself, yet in your mind as well.
Damn. This is some deep psychological stuff. Didn't expect that from a celestial.
A tragedy of meaning.
The darkness within her skull retracts as she waves her hand.
A man shakes his head after his drinking partner taps him on the shoulder.
Ask. If you are so adamant.
Where do you come from?
How did you meet Urth?
What was Urth like?
How long have you been here?
Why Darrow?
Do all celestials look like you?
M-"I'm not sure what else to ask."
I was crafted from molten blood.
Upon the slain corpse of the titan Wielokrwisty.
My sisters spawned from the flood, on the slope. At the Closing.
The Closing? So she is-
I am no Antesepalian. My crafting was made here, on this Esoteric Coast. Right as it all turned hellwards.
At least two millennia ago, then.
It was force I learned, so soon after my first light.
She lapses into more dated language when she recalls her birth.
She speaks of so many terms and strange concepts.
This is the life of a celestial.
That is where I come from. The eternal battle for the Holy Mountain.
Make a quick remark. It'll land!
So you're kind of a veteran?
You're... very old.
Antesep... what?
A short bark of a laugh in your mind.
Score.
She thinks you are being funny.
You could work with that.
I am young, by contrast.
One of the youngest among my kin.
Antesepalian, Cleric.
A term for those who were here before the closing of the Gates. During the Gate Era.
A colorful storm dances within the hole in her skull.
Those before me, they were the ones who actually arrived to this plane, they had not even a concept of time.
Many mortals say my presence is alien. Older celestials are alien to me.
She does not answer for quite some time.
Ominous.
At sea. I moved with an Ymian explorer at the time.
On her air ship.
Air ship? Like the Arcanist kind?
Ymian explorer?
(Let her continue.)
Yes. It was a slow and dangerous contraption.
Airships haven't made much progress since, due to the war.
You were not designed for flight.
Yes. You were designed for far more.
A somewhat human woman.
Perhaps a Japanese person.
Elaborate.
I will not.
I was an official Gold dispatch. My job was to watch the Ymian's movements and report my findings, while acting as an official witness.
After only a year of travel, the ship went down in the ocean. They accidentally flew into a frozen pocket.
Oh.
I stayed near to watch the disaster. As was my duty. To report.
She is quiet for a beat.
Twenty crewmembers died in the impact, and the other twelve gathered on the wreck.
They called out to me, pleading as they froze to death.
Oh fuck.
I did not have authority to interfere. As was the Golden Horde's foreign affair edicts at the time.
Her voice does not change in tone at all, yet you can feel the pain as she tells you this.
She obeyed.
She followed orders.
That is... good.
Horrible.
Once the voices were silent, I left the blizzard behind, moving inland.
You can just fly out in the Ocean?
That's... awful.
Why would you not attempt to save them?
(Keep your mouth shut.)
It was not easy.
I had orders.
Why listen to such bullshit orders?
(Just frown.)
She does not answer your burning question. Instead her voice simply echoes in your mind:
The storm raged.
Before making it out of the pocket, I was struck by lightning.
Lightning?
How'd you survive that?
(Keep quiet.)
Like a bolt? A bolt of lightning?
And you lived?
Yes, Cleric.
Her many eyes land upon her right arm, held out opposite the floating shards on her left.
That is when my wing broke. I fell into the depths.
Even an angel cannot withstand nature's fury.
That should have ended me. Yet the Strings aligned.
A fleet of humans were traveling across the rough Askanii waters.
You ran into the Chosen People?
Urth.
Chosen People.
She repeats your words.
She does not like that term.
The human god saved me.
That is how I met him.
I did not join him in his struggle with the low creatures of Dzikie Ziemie. Your Askanii.
Yet in time, I served.
You know.
You do.
You have your tales.
I know the stories. I want to know what you thought of him.
So he's a brave philosopher king, with a heart of gold?
(Shrug.)
You see many, many eyes gaze into yours.
She nods.
He was.
Meek.
Yes?
Ah. Other Meek. Sorry.
Kind.
Reluctant.
It was his weakness and his strength.
Your god was a complicated man, Cleric.
He did terrible things. He performed great deeds.
He was just a man.
He was a god.
Just a man, huh?
Is that your actual view of him?
A god of man.
She considers your question for a few seconds.
He built his city in his own image.
For good and ill.
I served him for a minuscule time.
Approximately forty-nine years.
So you fought trolls with Urth?
That's almost the entire existence of Norvik.
I'd say that's pretty long.
No. I joined after the initial conquest.
Almost.
We view time in different lights, Cleric. Remember that.
I am a senior member of the Urthguard.
The Patriarchs set my assignment. I am following orders.
She follows orders. Yet she rages inside. This is her struggle.
Oh yeah. It's weird, but she's really looking for some type of guidance here.
She is not capable of self-determination.
Not so far.
I head Nicholas Darrow's defense, along with a handful of rotating guards.
It is not a difficult appointment.
Must be boring.
Why listen to the Patriarchs?
Good. Serving Urth's legacy is honorable.
I am not searching for excitement.
Her many eyes look away, focusing on piles of documents scattered across the tower.
I have.
Nothing else to do.
That's sad.
You're looking for meaning.
Huh. Didn't expect an angel to be lost.
Sadness.
Meaning.
Lost.
She looks back at you.
Call it what you will.
I am here for now.
Do you believe them to be better?
No, of course not. But I figured an angel would think they are.
I thought they were all horrid brutes.
Brutes.
She repeats the word.
But you're clearly not. So maybe I'm wrong.
Their invasion of the Clanlands should be proof enough of that.
Brutes, yeah. Just like you.
Her many eyes look away from you.
Her many eyes glare at you.
The Horde consumes and subjugates. At times they fractionalize- splintering into deadly Warbands.
Usually by some divine mandate or plot, rather than similar motives to the civil wars of mortals.
Her telepathic voice changes to an octave lower than before.
I was a cog. Inside, I could not see the contraption. Outside, it is clear.
They are a machine. Built for a divine incursion. One ended millennia past.
She's a damn conchie? Didn't expect that.
You don't want to be a part of their war machine.
So you're a conchie?
So Norvik is better. I see.
(Just nod.)
Conchie.
What is that?
You know. Conscientious objector. You object to fighting in the war.
Conscientious objector.
That could be what I have turned out to be.
Better.
This city is not a machine. It is a living, breathing thing. One that may dance, or sing, or run off a cliff.
There is something good about that.
Freedom, baby.
She prefers the Urthfolkian way of life.
Who would not? Norvik is the greatest city on the Coast.
Too bad. (Smirk.)
She turns her head away from you.
Ah, come on, that was a decent line!
Dismissing your awkward comment? Good.
Eh. Probably the best you could hope for.
She liked the comment.
What? Really?
Nice.
Celestial creatures are amorphous spirits, built upon the energies of the positive.
We shape in time. We form by purpose. Some of us fast. Some of us slow. Some by physical means. Some by spiritual.
Unicorns are celestials.
That fact always pops up in your brain as soon as you hear the word celestials.
Celestials are even more diverse than their opposing devilish cousins.
From unicorns to couatls. From mighty empyreans to cherubs of Old Diminor.
She's pretty. Pretty angel.
R-"Well, I think you're pretty at least."
Cool, cool. Spiritual and physical both. Thanks for the info.
Not a single one of her many, many rotating eyes meet your gaze.
Aesthetic subjectivity was not in discussion, Cleric.
Please refrain from using such language.
She attempts to STIFLE your MANHOOD. It will not succeed!
Simply reiterate your position!
Oh. She did not hate that, did she?
Her reaction... is she flustered?
What? Did you just fluster an angel?!
I have the freedom to express my subjectivity as much as I want. I am a <shake>MAN</shake>!
Sorry. I got off-topic.
Ouch. My heart.
Freedom.
She considers the word carefully.
You made her go all philosophical. Geez.
She nods her head. "Yes. You did."
No. Problem.
Is she trying to be hip?
You are hurt.
She states the words less as a question, despite it being one.
Don't worry. Everything hurts a lot these days.
I'm fine. Don't you worry, sweetheart.
Sweet-heart.
SWEET-HEART?!
Why don't you call her a broad while you're at it?
Not actually. Do NOT do that.
You're welcome.
Not that she provided anything new or interesting.
She is silent for a moment. Then she gives you another calm nod.
You have not inquired about assistance.
Assistance?
The tea shop.
Oh right. I forgot.
Ah. Right. The job.
Can't go forgetting about the job.
You forgot about the tea shop?
It's the only reason you're here. It's your job, man.
Don't fuck up this paycheck too.
She descends slightly. You can almost look at her without bending your neck all the way back.
This incident is to be investigated entirely of your own accord, Cleric. I will not interfere.
However, my duties include keeping watch over the ruins. Miasto Głêbin: the City Below.
Are you entering the lower parts of Norvik?
I've done my fair share of spelunking, thank you very much.
Spelunking.
She is tasting your colorful use of language.
Good.
That is far. And dangerous.
If I find the time. I will assist you. Cleric. In the Undercoast Path.
Her voice betrays a certain feeling.
Deep within that radiant heart.
There has been interest in dealing with the dangers entering through that trail. It shall be dealt with, once and for all.
Glorious.
You.
She gawks at you, with all the eyes.
What did you do. With Gourgalash?
I'm here, aren't I? I defeated the beast.
(Dust your hands off.) "The big boy is kaput."
Impressive, Cleric. This will be reported.
You are such a MAN.
(Give her a thumbs up.)
Still.
She stares at you. With many eyes.
What kind of dangers?
I like dangers. It's, uh, my middle name. But in singular.
I don't like the sound of that.
Monsters.
Her voice implies an added 'obviously, you little prick'.
Even when explaining things she may feel are obvious, she has an immense amount of patience.
She's used to dealing with things less intelligent than herself. You can relate.
Patience is not always borne out of low expectations.
It is not.
Correct.
The angel is incorrect.
No. Hold on.
The angel is correct. Your middle name is not actually Dangers.
Eh, joke didn't land. Don't chase it.
Wise.
Thanks?
Is it?
The angel does not nod.
She continues, "Enemies of the state. The type that festers."
They are many. You will need to be wary.
Meek see many bad thing come from dungeon. Always bad thing...
Angel is scary. This will help.
All from dark is scared of burning light!
Your scarf then whispers to you, "Meek include self in list."
I will meet you there.
An angel will surely help out a lot.
What's that, like, a third companion?
What's that, your second companion?
At this rate, you'll have a full party in no time.
She will be a good support.
Good, you can send her in to deal with the monsters below.
Don't think an angel like that would steal any loot for herself, either. So it's really an optimal solution.
You have a goddess on your side.
Is this on behalf of Darrow?
That's kind of you. I really need the help.
I... okay. Sure.
(Just stare at her and her many eyes that do not meet your gaze at all.)
It is on my behalf.
I assumed so.
Rude.
Blunt. You like that. Even if it hurts.
The angel returns to her work.
You hear the goblin mutter as he sneaks back into the tower.
You're alive? Cool. Good.
Ettir will now join you in the Undercoast Path, as long as you do not go down there solo.
No. No...
There is no way you're talking to this woman.
She is treating you with disrespect, bad attitude, and rudeness.
And it is getting to you. Burrowing holes in your manhood.
Holes?
Yes, HOLES!
This is ridiculous.
Just because she's an angel doesn't mean she can ignore your questions.
You need to be firm. Show her that you're a MAN.
(Gulp.) "...A man?"
A man, she repeats.
You said that out loud?!
Hm? What?
You are speaking.
Stop fumbling this opportunity. Show her! Show her why she can trust you. As a MAN.
